question: What is the medical term for inflammation of the fallopian tubes?
explanation: Salpingitis simply means infection and inflammation in one or both of the fallopian tubes. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h1)

question: Where does fertilization of the egg normally take place in the female reproductive tract?
explanation: The ampulla is the wider middle part of the fallopian tube where the sperm and egg usually meet. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h1)

question: What is the most common cause of salpingitis?
explanation: Infections like Chlamydia and Gonorrhea are the main culprits behind most fallopian tube infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h2)

question: How do infectious bacteria usually travel to cause salpingitis?

options.A: They enter directly through the skin of the lower abdomen
options.B: They spread through the bloodstream from the lungs
options.C: They ascend upward from the lower genital tract
options.D: They travel down from the abdominal cavity through the liver

explanation: Salpingitis is an ascending infection, meaning germs travel up from the vagina and cervix into the uterus and tubes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h2)

question: Why does scarring often develop inside the fallopian tubes after an infection?

options.A: Excess hormones thicken the muscular walls
options.B: Blood clots block the internal blood vessels
options.C: Calcium deposits harden the ciliated lining

explanation: Just like a skin wound forms a scar as it heals, inflamed tubal tissue can form fibrous bands that narrow or block the tube. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h3)

question: A patient had severe, untreated salpingitis a year ago. What long-term change is most likely in her fallopian tubes now?

options.A: Thinned muscle walls and widened openings
options.B: Enlarged and overly active cilia hairs
options.C: Narrowed lumens and scar tissue adhesions

explanation: Past severe inflammation leaves behind scar tissue that can narrow the inside passageway (lumen) of the tube. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h3)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of acute salpingitis?

options.B: Sharp pain in the upper right shoulder

explanation: Inflammation of the tubes usually causes lower belly and pelvic pain on both sides. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h4)

question: Why might a patient with chlamydial salpingitis delay seeing a doctor?

options.A: The symptoms can be very mild and easy to ignore
options.B: The primary sign is complete loss of appetite
options.C: It causes immediate paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: It only produces symptoms during pregnancy

explanation: Chlamydia infections can be sneaky, causing mild symptoms that patients might brush off until bigger problems pop up. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h4)

question: What physical exam finding is typically linked to pelvic infections like salpingitis?

options.A: Painless rigidity of the abdominal wall
options.D: Absent bowel sounds in all quadrants

explanation: During a pelvic exam, moving the cervix stretches those inflamed tissues, causing sharp pain. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h5)

question: Why would a doctor order a transvaginal ultrasound for a patient with suspected salpingitis?

options.A: To visualize fluid-filled tubes or pelvic abscesses
options.B: To check the openness of the cervical opening
options.C: To confirm the presence of early pregnancy
options.D: To measure hormone levels in the bloodstream

explanation: Ultrasounds are great for peeking inside to check for swelling, fluid buildup, or abscesses in the tubes and ovaries. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h5)

question: Why are broad-spectrum antibiotics started immediately before lab test results come back?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any follow-up blood tests
options.B: To prevent the patient from experiencing allergic reactions
options.C: To prevent rapid progression and permanent tubal damage
options.D: To destroy normal vaginal flora permanently

explanation: Acting fast stops the infection in its tracks, helping to protect the tubes from long-term damage. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h6)

question: Which situation usually requires admitting a patient to the hospital for IV antibiotics?

options.A: A positive Chlamydia swab with normal vital signs
options.B: Spotting between menstrual periods without pain
options.C: Presence of high fever and a suspected tubo-ovarian abscess
options.D: Mild lower abdominal discomfort lasting two days

explanation: High fever and abscesses mean the infection is serious and needs inpatient care and IV medications. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h6)

question: A hospitalized patient has acute salpingitis with pelvic pain and a mild fever. Which nursing position helps drain pelvic fluids downward?

options.A: Ice packs applied directly to the lower abdomen
options.B: Strict bed rest flat on her back

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Keeping the patient slightly upright helps infected fluids pool safely in the lower pelvis rather than spreading upward. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h7)

question: What is the most important instruction for a patient going home with oral antibiotics for salpingitis?

options.A: Only treat your partner if they develop a fever
options.B: Resume sexual activity immediately if you feel fine
options.C: Stop taking the pills as soon as your belly pain stops
options.D: Finish all the medication even if you start feeling better

explanation: Always remind patients to finish their full course of antibiotics so the infection doesn't bounce back stronger! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h7)

question: What is a major long-term risk for a woman who has had repeated bouts of salpingitis?

options.A: Chronic swelling of the lower legs

explanation: Scars from repeated infections can block the tubes, making it harder to get pregnant or increasing the risk of an ectopic pregnancy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h8)

question: Why can tubal damage from salpingitis lead to an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Damaged cilia cannot properly propel the fertilized egg to the uterus
options.B: Hormone levels drop so low that the uterus rejects the embryo
options.C: The ovaries release eggs too rapidly for the uterus to prepare
options.D: The uterine lining becomes too thick for any implantation

explanation: The tiny hair-like cilia inside the tube get damaged by the infection, so they can't sweep the fertilized egg down to the uterus as they normally would. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h8)
